content.thinking: I've confirmed the key findings: PR 9's --add-dir usage and blocked-state handling break the reviewer flow as PR 11 experienced live, while PR 10 and PR 11's smoke sessions check out against on-disk artifacts, and PR 10's version bump is incompatible with main's adapter. I now have enough verified evidence to proceed with scoring.

input.summary: I mapped PRD_REVIEWER_PANE's six work items, eight design-table rows and four acceptance bullets (plus the section-5 live-smoke merge gate) to each branch's code, diffed all four PRDs against main per branch, verified the smoke-test claims against `claude agents --all`, transcripts and run directories, and checked `claude --help` for the variadic-option defect. PR 10 is the only one that does slice A as specified (binds the reviewer session UUID, extends both attach_panels and attach-one, runs the gating smoke test twice with artifacts on disk) and records every deviation in the PRDs; its lapse is bundling B/C pre-run work into A's PR, which leaves new runs unviewable (export 1.2.0 vs main's z.literal('1.0.0')) until B's run merges, and it says so. PR 11 verifies slice A most thoroughly (four live sessions covering deadline, fail-closed and accept paths, plus the variadic --add-dir fix) and records deviations best, but it overrides the umbrella PRD's explicit delivery plan by implementing B and C directly in a 56-file/+6074 diff, ships vestigial feature directories that would assign already-done work, and hand-writes the completion schema outside the repo's contract convention. PR 9 has perfect scope discipline and is candid that the merge gate was skipped, but its native path is broken on first launch (prompt swallowed by variadic --add-dir; write denied under dontAsk with no allow rule) and it silently fails acceptance bullet 2 by treating a reviewer that asks a question as fatal, while its README claims the opposite. Ranking on this dimension: PR 10 > PR 11 > PR 9.

input.ranking_reason: PR 10 is the only branch that does slice A as written (session-UUID binding, third pane in both attach_panels and attach-one, print fallback, smoke test run and recorded) and confines its extra work to the pre-run items the B/C PRDs themselves list, with every deviation logged; its export-version gap is real but disclosed and is partly the PRD's own design. PR 11 meets and exceeds every slice-A acceptance bullet with the most live evidence and the most complete decisions log, but it overrode the umbrella PRD's explicit "A, then B's run, then C's run" plan and its stated rationale, delivering the large multi-slice diff the PRD argued against, replacing the repo's independent-reviewer process for B/C with a self-run audit, shipping feature directories that would assign already-done work, and hand-writing the completion schema outside the contract convention. PR 9 has exemplary scope discipline and is honest about skipping the smoke test, but that skipped gate is exactly what the PRD says catches launch-time failures, and PR 9 has three of them (prompt swallowed by variadic --add-dir, write denied under dontAsk with no allow rule, blocked state treated as fatal); the last silently fails acceptance bullet 2 while its README claims the opposite, and the launch_token binding contradicts the PRD table it left untouched.

findings.title: Prompt placed after variadic --add-dir; native reviewer starts with no task
findings.detail: run_reviewer builds the command as `--tools … --permission-mode dontAsk --add-dir <run> <prompt>`. On this host's CLI the --add-dir option is variadic, so the positional prompt is consumed as a second directory and the session starts idle. PR 11 reproduced exactly this live (attempt 1 failed in seven seconds) on the same CLI version and reordered its arguments; PR 10 avoided it by placing --add-dir before --tools. PR 9's launch test asserts the value after --add-dir but never the prompt's position, so offline tests cannot see it. This is the class of launch-time failure PRD §5 says the (skipped) smoke test exists to catch.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:217-220: `command = [self.executable, "--bg", "--name", …, "--tools", self.reviewer_tools, "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt]`. `claude --help` (2.1.278): `--add-dir <directories...>  Additional directories to allow tool access to`. Test /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/test_interactive.py:171-193 pins `command[command.index("--add-dir") + 1] == str(self.directory)` only. PR 11's fix and pin: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:220-226 and test_interactive.py:245-249 (`command[-3:-1] == ["--permission-mode", "dontAsk"]`).

findings.title: Reviewer asking a question is fatal, contradicting acceptance bullet 2 and PR 9's own docs
findings.detail: PRD §5 bullet 2: 'A reviewer that stops to ask a question can be answered in the pane, and the run resumes when the completion file appears and the session goes idle.' PR 9's wait_review raises the moment the native session reports state `blocked`, and its test codifies that. Both PR 10 and PR 11 observed live that `blocked` is precisely the state a reviewer enters when it ends a turn asking a person something (or when a write is refused). PR 9's feature README nonetheless tells the operator they can answer the reviewer's question in the pane. Not recorded as a deviation anywhere.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:207-208: `if row["state"] == "blocked": raise RuntimeError("Reviewer blocked; inspect quota or native error. No billing/provider fallback.")`. Test test_automatic.py:254-262 `test_a_missing_or_blocked_reviewer_stops_rather_than_relaunching` asserts the raise. Docs claim: features/project-workflows/README.md (PR 9 diff): 'you can answer a question the reviewer asks there'. Live observation: PR 10 handoff attempt 1 ('ended its turn asking a person … `claude agents` reported the session as `blocked`'); PR 11 handoff attempt 1. Contrast PR 10 automatic.py:208-210 and PR 11 automatic.py:219-223, both of which note it once and keep waiting.

findings.title: Merge gate (PRD §5 controlled live smoke test) skipped; three launch-time defects follow
findings.detail: PRD_REVIEWER_PANE §5: 'Before merging, run one controlled live smoke test … This catches the launch-time failures (late pid, pane not ready) that the first live run showed offline tests do not.' PR 9 says plainly it did not run it (PRD status, handoff 'Not done', PR body item 2). The consequence is concrete: the variadic --add-dir defect, the Write-denied-under-dontAsk defect (PR 9 has no --allowedTools rule; both PR 10 and PR 11 measured live that dontAsk denies the write without an `Edit(//path)` rule), and the blocked-is-fatal defect were all found by the other two PRs' smoke runs within minutes. Honest, but the PRD's stated precondition for merging is unmet and the shipped native path does not work.
findings.evidence: docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:60 (main). PR 9 PRD status line: 'the controlled live smoke test in section 5 has **not** been run'. /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/docs/HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md 'Not done' section. interactive.py:184-185 `reviewer_tools = "Read,Glob,Grep,Write"`, `reviewer_permission_mode = "dontAsk"`, no `--allowedTools` anywhere in the command (217-220). PR 10 handoff: 'had its Write to review.completion.json denied twice ("Permission to use Write has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode")'.

findings.title: Completion file binds launch_token but PRD design table still says reviewer session UUID
findings.detail: The PRD's 'Bound to' row names the reviewer session UUID. PR 9's schema and read_review_completion bind a controller-issued launch_token instead (independence is checked separately against bundle snapshot UUIDs). PR 9's RUNBOOK table says 'launch token', its handoff mentions it, but docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md's row was left unchanged, so the PRD and RUNBOOK now disagree within the same branch. PR 11 made the same design choice but rewrote the PRD row with a dated rationale; PR 10 followed the PRD literally.

RUNBOOK (PR 9 diff): '| Bound to | run id, the `review` node, the bundle SHA-256, the candidate commit and the launch token issued for this session |'. `git diff 61e4752 feature-opus -- docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md` touches only the status line, §6 and a new §7.

findings.detail: Work item 3 and §3 say 'attach_panels and attach-one gain a third pane'. PR 9 adds attach-one --node reviewer and a separate attach_reviewer_pane called by the review node, but attach_panels is unchanged for the reviewer, so an operator who runs `attach` after the review node has started gets two panes. Recorded in PRD §6 with the reasoning that the session does not exist at start. PR 10 (launched_nodes) and PR 11 (attach_panels checks review.interactive.json) both cover both entry points.

findings.title: Prompt instructs an impossible atomic temp-file-then-rename write
findings.detail: The reviewer has only Read/Glob/Grep/Write and no Bash; it cannot rename a file, and under dontAsk a temp-file write would be denied even with a single-path allow rule. PR 11's prompt explicitly says the file cannot be written under a temporary name and renamed. Another symptom of never exercising the prompt live.

Contrast /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:175-176: 'It cannot be written under a temporary name and renamed, so write it once, complete, as your last action'.

findings.title: Deadline does not stop the reviewer, departing from 'same lifecycle as workers'; recorded
findings.detail: PRD §1/§2 ask for the same lifecycle as workers, and workers are stopped when their deadline expires. PR 9 raises at the deadline but leaves the reviewer running for the operator to stop. Justified in the handoff (an idle reviewer consumes no usage) and stated in the RUNBOOK recovery entry, so class (a). PR 10 and PR 11 stop it.

Handoff 'Decisions and deviations': 'A deadline does not stop the reviewer.' automatic.py:202-203 raises without stop; the BaseException handler (288-292) only updates the receipt. Contrast PR 10 automatic.py:305-313 and PR 11 automatic.py:349-356.

findings.title: Exact scope discipline, repo-convention contract, and candid status reporting
findings.detail: PR 9 touches only the slice-A file set the PRD names, defines reviewCompletion in v1.ts with examples and negative contract tests and generates the JSON via the repo's export script, ticks the three-pane open question in both PRDs, adds an explicit PRD §7 note for the Write-tool deviation, and states in the PRD status line, handoff and PR body that the smoke gate was not run. Its handoff also documents three mutation checks. That transparency is exactly what the dimension asks for, even though the delivered behaviour falls short.

HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md 'Mutation checks' table.

PR 10 ships A plus both slices' pre-run tables (contracts/projects reviewResult 1.1.0 and runInputs 1.2.0, export 1.2.0, `workflow export`, two feature directories) in one squashed commit, doing C's pre-run work before B has even been launched. findings.detail: wait_review accepts the file when the session is idle, done or blocked; the PRD's 'Accepted when' row and PR 10's RUNBOOK sentence both say idle or done. findings.title: Prompt placed after variadic --add-dir; native reviewer starts with no task
findings.detail: run_reviewer builds the command as `--tools … --permission-mode dontAsk --add-dir <run> <prompt>`. On this host's CLI the --add-dir option is variadic, so the positional prompt is consumed as a second directory and the session starts idle. PR 11 reproduced exactly this live (attempt 1 failed in seven seconds) on the same CLI version and reordered its arguments; PR 10 avoided it by placing --add-dir before --tools. PR 9's launch test asserts the value after --add-dir but never the prompt's position, so offline tests cannot see it. This is the class of launch-time failure PRD §5 says the (skipped) smoke test exists to catch.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:217-220: `command = [self.executable, "--bg", "--name", …, "--tools", self.reviewer_tools, "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt]`. `claude --help` (2.1.278): `--add-dir <directories...>  Additional directories to allow tool access to`. Test /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/test_interactive.py:171-193 pins `command[command.index("--add-dir") + 1] == str(self.directory)` only. PR 11's fix and pin: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:220-226 and test_interactive.py:245-249 (`command[-3:-1] == ["--permission-mode", "dontAsk"]`).

findings.title: Reviewer asking a question is fatal, contradicting acceptance bullet 2 and PR 9's own docs
findings.detail: PRD §5 bullet 2: 'A reviewer that stops to ask a question can be answered in the pane, and the run resumes when the completion file appears and the session goes idle.' PR 9's wait_review raises the moment the native session reports state `blocked`, and its test codifies that. Both PR 10 and PR 11 observed live that `blocked` is precisely the state a reviewer enters when it ends a turn asking a person something (or when a write is refused). PR 9's feature README nonetheless tells the operator they can answer the reviewer's question in the pane. Not recorded as a deviation anywhere.

Docs claim: features/project-workflows/README.md (PR 9 diff): 'you can answer a question the reviewer asks there'. findings.title: Spec-literal UUID binding relies on the reviewer knowing its own session id; a mis-copy ends the run

Every PR resolves it by granting Write, and every PR writes the deviation down (PR 9 in a new PRD §7, PR 10 in PRD §6 plus the umbrella log, PR 11 in the umbrella log and RUNBOOK). PR 10 and PR 11 additionally constrain it to one path with `--allowedTools "Edit(//<run>/review.completion.json)"` after measuring live that a `Write(...)` rule never matches; PR 9 grants Write with no allow rule under dontAsk, which the other two showed is denied.

data.summary: I mapped PRD_REVIEWER_PANE's six work items, eight design-table rows and four acceptance bullets (plus the section-5 live-smoke merge gate) to each branch's code, diffed all four PRDs against main per branch, verified the smoke-test claims against `claude agents --all`, transcripts and run directories, and checked `claude --help` for the variadic-option defect. PR 10 is the only one that does slice A as specified (binds the reviewer session UUID, extends both attach_panels and attach-one, runs the gating smoke test twice with artifacts on disk) and records every deviation in the PRDs; its lapse is bundling B/C pre-run work into A's PR, which leaves new runs unviewable (export 1.2.0 vs main's z.literal('1.0.0')) until B's run merges, and it says so. PR 11 verifies slice A most thoroughly (four live sessions covering deadline, fail-closed and accept paths, plus the variadic --add-dir fix) and records deviations best, but it overrides the umbrella PRD's explicit delivery plan by implementing B and C directly in a 56-file/+6074 diff, ships vestigial feature directories that would assign already-done work, and hand-writes the completion schema outside the repo's contract convention. PR 9 has perfect scope discipline and is candid that the merge gate was skipped, but its native path is broken on first launch (prompt swallowed by variadic --add-dir; write denied under dontAsk with no allow rule) and it silently fails acceptance bullet 2 by treating a reviewer that asks a question as fatal, while its README claims the opposite. Ranking on this dimension: PR 10 > PR 11 > PR 9.
data.pr9: Scope: exactly slice A (21 files; workflow +931/-113, contracts +174, docs +73, no server/src). Work items: WI1 DONE the repo way (contracts/workflow/v1.ts:94-106 zod + generated reviewCompletion.schema.json + examples + contract.test.ts:56-78), but binds `launch_token`, not the PRD's reviewer session UUID. WI2 PARTIAL: native_review (automatic.py:254-293), wait_review (196-212) mirrors wait_handoffs so literally that native state `blocked` raises (207-208), schema validation via validate_schema (183), bundle/worktree/evidence re-checks (272-277), identity-checked stop (281, pipeline.py:149-154), print kept behind --reviewer-transport (249-250, pinned at prepare). WI3 PARTIAL: attach-one --node reviewer (interactive.py:396) and attach_reviewer_pane (355-381) called from the review node; attach_panels (295-330) does not gain a third pane, recorded as a design choice in PRD §6. WI4 DONE (pipeline.py:156-170 receipt via run_reviewer + "Reviewer session <uuid> in <worktree>" event, review/detached when no tab). WI5 DONE offline: FakeSessions reviewer (test_automatic.py:371-390), four real processes [75,130,75,0] with a mid-review interrupt (392-442), foreign bundle (476-497), wrong token/candidate/schema (196-236), no-file timeout (498-516), PrintReviewerTests. WI6 DONE (RUNBOOK section + recovery entry, feature README "The reviewer pane", INTERACTIVE_SESSIONS, VALIDATION, contracts README). Design rows: completion file ✓; bound-to ✗ (launch_token; docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:26 still says "reviewer session UUID" while its own RUNBOOK table says "launch token"); payload ✓; accepted-when ✓ idle/done; timeout ✓ 1800 from launch_requested_at; independence ✓ (269-270 vs bundle snapshots); human input ✗ (blocked kills the run); after-acceptance ✓; tools ✗ Read,Glob,Grep,Write with NO allow rule and dontAsk (interactive.py:184-185, 219) — recorded in PRD §7; no MCP ✓; --add-dir ✓ but placed immediately before the prompt (217-220), and `claude --help` shows `--add-dir <directories...>` is variadic, so the prompt is swallowed. Acceptance §5: live smoke ✗ (skipped; stated in PRD status, handoff "Not done", PR body); bullet 1 offline only; bullet 2 ✗ by code (and features/project-workflows/README.md claims "you can answer a question the reviewer asks there"); bullet 3 ✓ offline; bullet 4 ✓ offline, but the reviewer is deliberately not stopped at the deadline (RUNBOOK: "not stopped for you"), recorded. Prompt also instructs "write atomically (temporary file then rename)" (automatic.py:168), impossible with its tool set. Deviation classes: Write tool (a), pane-not-in-attach_panels (a), deadline-no-stop (a), transport pinned (a), no smoke test (a, very honest), launch_token binding (b: handoff mentions it, PRD table untouched), blocked-is-fatal (b: silent, contradicted by its docs), --add-dir order (undetected). Net: disciplined and honest about what it did not do, but the delivered native path fails on first live launch and the PRD's stated merge gate is unmet.
data.pr10: Scope: slice A in full plus B/C "pre-run work" (39 files; workflow +1232/-187, contracts +1393, features +607, docs +97; no server/src). Work items: WI1 DONE the repo way (v1.ts:99-116 with reviewer_session regex, generated schema, examples, contract.test.ts:56-73) and it is the only PR that binds what the PRD table says (reviewer session UUID). WI2 DONE: review_candidate dispatch (automatic.py:228-261), review_native (282-317) launch → event → pane → wait_review → stop_session with identity check (298-301) → finish_review re-hashing bundle/patch (264-278); read_review_completion validates against the committed contracts/workflow JSON (130-131, 173-187) and rejects a worker UUID; print path shares finish_review (319-353); transport from plan (43-45). WI3 DONE verbatim: attach_panels grows to three panes via launched_nodes (interactive.py:225, 280-327), attach_reviewer_pane splits off the adapter pane (343-371), attach-one --node review (384). WI4 DONE in substance (receipt from interactive.launch; events at automatic.py:289-296 rather than pipeline.py). WI5 DONE: accepted-and-stopped (test_automatic.py:375-391), wrong bundle fails closed (393-411), blocked verdict recorded (413-422), idle-to-deadline then stopped (424-439), interrupt leaves reviewer running (441-455), multi-process with one reviewer interruption (457-500), WaitReviewTests incl. worker-posing-as-reviewer and blocked-is-waiting (527-577); print tests pinned to transport=print. WI6 DONE: RUNBOOK "Automatic review session" (pane, Edit-rule explanation, protocol, deadline, `claude --resume` path), feature README, INTERACTIVE_SESSIONS. Design rows: all ✓ except tools (Write allow-listed to one path via `--allowedTools "Edit(//<run>/review.completion.json)"`, interactive.py:182-186; recorded in PRD §6 and umbrella log) and accepted-when (also accepts in state `blocked`, automatic.py:211, while its own RUNBOOK says "only once the session is idle or done"). Prompt order is safe (prompt follows --permission-mode). Acceptance §5: live smoke ✓ twice, verified on disk (~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/smoke/review-smoke-001: automatic-review.json session 5865c9a6, status blocked, error "Independent reviewer blocked the candidate"; `claude agents --all` lists dccd22b5 stopped and 5865c9a6 done in that review-worktree); attempt 1 found the Write/Edit rule family and the blocked state; bullet 1 ✓ live; bullet 2 ~ (blocked=waiting implemented, no question asked live); bullet 3 ✓ offline; bullet 4 ✓ offline, reviewer stopped. Beyond A: contracts/projects reviewResult 1.1.0 + runInputs 1.2.0 (v1.ts:66,120), export_state 1.2.0 (export_state.py:16), `workflow export` + test_export.py (7 tests incl. re-export of a 1.0.0 copy), features/review-result and run-inputs with policies/tasks, launch FEATURES — every row of PRD_REVIEW_RESULT §2 and PRD_RUN_INPUTS §3 pre-run tables. Deviation classes: Write allow-list (a, PRD §6 + umbrella), blocked=waiting (a, PRD §6), legacy plans default print (a, RUNBOOK/handoff; prepare pins native for new runs), task-display decision made in A's PR (a, umbrella + C §7), B/C pre-run bundled and C's pre-run done before B merged (a, handoff "Suggested commits"), viewer gap for new 1.2.0 runs (a, PR body "New runs export at 1.2.0 until B's adapter lands"), accept-in-blocked (b, only in a test comment; RUNBOOK contradicts). Net: the closest to "what was asked, the way it was asked", with the gate met and deviations logged; its one real cost is the self-inflicted export/adapter gap.
data.pr11: Scope: all three slices implemented directly (56 files; workflow +2057/-177, server +756, src +874, tests +970, contracts +991, features +337). Work items: WI1 ~ hand-written contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json (39 lines) with no v1.ts zod, examples or contract test; contracts/workflow/README.md:12 admits "hand-written, not generated from v1.ts", contrary to that README's own rule that v1.ts is authoritative and *.schema.json is generated; binds `launch_token`. WI2 DONE and hardened: review_candidate (automatic.py:229-266) incl. stop-retry on resume, _review_native (292-323) with launch-window interrupt handling, _accept_native (326-365) re-checking identity/independence/worktree/evidence, wait_review (204-227) idle/done only with blocked as attention, read_review_completion via validate_schema (181-201), _decide records review.json for every verdict and downgrades approved-with-P0/P1 to blocked (275-289), print path (367-405). WI3 DONE: attach_panels adds the reviewer pane to an existing tab (interactive.py:288-296) and to a new one (335-336), attach_reviewer_panel (362-384), attach-one --node review (399). WI4 DONE (pipeline.py:148-166 receipt, event with UUID, best-effort pane gated on HERDR_ENV=1 like main's other Herdr controls; reconcile_reviewer 168-181). WI5 DONE and broadest: native session recorded (test_automatic.py:489-521), four-process [75,130,75,0] reviewer interrupt (523-575), wrong bundle/token/candidate/keys, blocked verdict, unresolved P1 (590-607), identity/independence/worktree/evidence/deadline refusals (752-782), print tests (440-487), launch-order pin (test_interactive.py:245-249). WI6 DONE (RUNBOOK "Automatic mode: the review step" with resume path and export, feature README, workflow/README, contracts/workflow/README). Design rows: all ✓ except bound-to (launch_token; docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:26 rewritten in place with rationale and date, plus umbrella log) and tools (Write of exactly one path via Edit(//…) rule, interactive.py:223-226; umbrella log + RUNBOOK; §1/§3 prose "Read, Glob, Grep" left unchanged). Acceptance §5: live smoke ✓ four sessions, verified (`claude agents --all`: 7eb01f17 stopped, a4c348e5/25d99bf4/f36b923d done in the scratchpad smoke-run worktree; automatic-review.json succeeded with session f36b923d, review.json approved with 8 findings all carrying worker/requirement, review.stop.json stopped:true); bullet 1 ✓ live; bullet 2 ~ (blocked=waiting, no question asked); bullet 3 ✓ offline; bullet 4 ✓ live (attempt 2 hit the deadline, stopped, no second reviewer). Beyond A: B and C in full — server/projects.ts EXPORT_VERSIONS 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0 (:44,:145) so the live run keeps loading, reviews/inputs routes, src/projects panels, all nine PRD scenario ids as browser tests (review.spec.ts:27,97,134,155; inputs.spec.ts:30,98,177,226,251, C's paths-redacted renamed inputs-paths-redacted), export 1.2.0 + `workflow export`, verbatim rate measured 8/8 and recorded in PRD_RUN_INPUTS §7. Deviation classes: direct implementation instead of feature runs (a, PRD statuses + handoff §1, but against umbrella §2's explicit order and rationale and B's "so this run's own review exercises the reviewer pane live"), launch_token (a, borderline c: table row rewritten), Write (a), reviewResult at 1.2.0 not 1.1.0 (a, handoff §6), approved→blocked rewrite (a), nullable transport (a), findings grouping (a), hand-written schema (a, README only), feature dirs described as "not an implementation" while the implementation is in the tree (b: misleading if launched), scratch smoke run reusing run_id project-workflows-001 (b, low). Net: best slice-A verification and recording, worst adherence to the delivery plan the PRD author wrote down.
data.ranking_reason: PR 10 is the only branch that does slice A as written (session-UUID binding, third pane in both attach_panels and attach-one, print fallback, smoke test run and recorded) and confines its extra work to the pre-run items the B/C PRDs themselves list, with every deviation logged; its export-version gap is real but disclosed and is partly the PRD's own design. PR 11 meets and exceeds every slice-A acceptance bullet with the most live evidence and the most complete decisions log, but it overrode the umbrella PRD's explicit "A, then B's run, then C's run" plan and its stated rationale, delivering the large multi-slice diff the PRD argued against, replacing the repo's independent-reviewer process for B/C with a self-run audit, shipping feature directories that would assign already-done work, and hand-writing the completion schema outside the contract convention. PR 9 has exemplary scope discipline and is honest about skipping the smoke test, but that skipped gate is exactly what the PRD says catches launch-time failures, and PR 9 has three of them (prompt swallowed by variadic --add-dir, write denied under dontAsk with no allow rule, blocked state treated as fatal); the last silently fails acceptance bullet 2 while its README claims the opposite, and the launch_token binding contradicts the PRD table it left untouched.

findings.title: Prompt placed after variadic --add-dir; native reviewer starts with no task
findings.detail: run_reviewer builds the command as `--tools … --permission-mode dontAsk --add-dir <run> <prompt>`. On this host's CLI the --add-dir option is variadic, so the positional prompt is consumed as a second directory and the session starts idle. PR 11 reproduced exactly this live (attempt 1 failed in seven seconds) on the same CLI version and reordered its arguments; PR 10 avoided it by placing --add-dir before --tools. PR 9's launch test asserts the value after --add-dir but never the prompt's position, so offline tests cannot see it. This is the class of launch-time failure PRD §5 says the (skipped) smoke test exists to catch.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:217-220: `command = [self.executable, "--bg", "--name", …, "--tools", self.reviewer_tools, "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt]`. `claude --help` (2.1.278): `--add-dir <directories...>  Additional directories to allow tool access to`. Test /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/test_interactive.py:171-193 pins `command[command.index("--add-dir") + 1] == str(self.directory)` only. PR 11's fix and pin: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/interactive.py:220-226 and test_interactive.py:245-249 (`command[-3:-1] == ["--permission-mode", "dontAsk"]`).

findings.title: Reviewer asking a question is fatal, contradicting acceptance bullet 2 and PR 9's own docs
findings.detail: PRD §5 bullet 2: 'A reviewer that stops to ask a question can be answered in the pane, and the run resumes when the completion file appears and the session goes idle.' PR 9's wait_review raises the moment the native session reports state `blocked`, and its test codifies that. Both PR 10 and PR 11 observed live that `blocked` is precisely the state a reviewer enters when it ends a turn asking a person something (or when a write is refused). PR 9's feature README nonetheless tells the operator they can answer the reviewer's question in the pane. Not recorded as a deviation anywhere.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:207-208: `if row["state"] == "blocked": raise RuntimeError("Reviewer blocked; inspect quota or native error. No billing/provider fallback.")`. Test test_automatic.py:254-262 `test_a_missing_or_blocked_reviewer_stops_rather_than_relaunching` asserts the raise. Docs claim: features/project-workflows/README.md (PR 9 diff): 'you can answer a question the reviewer asks there'. Live observation: PR 10 handoff attempt 1 ('ended its turn asking a person … `claude agents` reported the session as `blocked`'); PR 11 handoff attempt 1. Contrast PR 10 automatic.py:208-210 and PR 11 automatic.py:219-223, both of which note it once and keep waiting.

findings.title: Merge gate (PRD §5 controlled live smoke test) skipped; three launch-time defects follow
findings.detail: PRD_REVIEWER_PANE §5: 'Before merging, run one controlled live smoke test … This catches the launch-time failures (late pid, pane not ready) that the first live run showed offline tests do not.' PR 9 says plainly it did not run it (PRD status, handoff 'Not done', PR body item 2). The consequence is concrete: the variadic --add-dir defect, the Write-denied-under-dontAsk defect (PR 9 has no --allowedTools rule; both PR 10 and PR 11 measured live that dontAsk denies the write without an `Edit(//path)` rule), and the blocked-is-fatal defect were all found by the other two PRs' smoke runs within minutes. Honest, but the PRD's stated precondition for merging is unmet and the shipped native path does not work.
findings.evidence: docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:60 (main). PR 9 PRD status line: 'the controlled live smoke test in section 5 has **not** been run'. /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/docs/HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md 'Not done' section. interactive.py:184-185 `reviewer_tools = "Read,Glob,Grep,Write"`, `reviewer_permission_mode = "dontAsk"`, no `--allowedTools` anywhere in the command (217-220). PR 10 handoff: 'had its Write to review.completion.json denied twice ("Permission to use Write has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode")'.

findings.title: Completion file binds launch_token but PRD design table still says reviewer session UUID
findings.detail: The PRD's 'Bound to' row names the reviewer session UUID. PR 9's schema and read_review_completion bind a controller-issued launch_token instead (independence is checked separately against bundle snapshot UUIDs). PR 9's RUNBOOK table says 'launch token', its handoff mentions it, but docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md's row was left unchanged, so the PRD and RUNBOOK now disagree within the same branch. PR 11 made the same design choice but rewrote the PRD row with a dated rationale; PR 10 followed the PRD literally.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:26 (unchanged from main): `| Bound to | run id, `review` node, bundle SHA-256, candidate commit, reviewer session UUID |`. contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json (PR 9): required includes `launch_token`, no `reviewer_session`. automatic.py:184-185: `item["launch_token"] != token`. RUNBOOK (PR 9 diff): '| Bound to | run id, the `review` node, the bundle SHA-256, the candidate commit and the launch token issued for this session |'. `git diff 61e4752 feature-opus -- docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md` touches only the status line, §6 and a new §7.

findings.title: Third pane not added to attach_panels (work item 3), recorded as a design choice
findings.detail: Work item 3 and §3 say 'attach_panels and attach-one gain a third pane'. PR 9 adds attach-one --node reviewer and a separate attach_reviewer_pane called by the review node, but attach_panels is unchanged for the reviewer, so an operator who runs `attach` after the review node has started gets two panes. Recorded in PRD §6 with the reasoning that the session does not exist at start. PR 10 (launched_nodes) and PR 11 (attach_panels checks review.interactive.json) both cover both entry points.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:295-330 attach_panels iterates NODES only; 355-381 attach_reviewer_pane; 396 `--node choices=[*NODES, REVIEWER]`. PR 9 PRD §6: 'this is `attach_reviewer_pane`, called by the review node, rather than a third pane in `attach_panels`'. Contrast PR 10 interactive.py:225,280-327 and PR 11 interactive.py:288-296,335-336.

findings.title: Prompt instructs an impossible atomic temp-file-then-rename write
findings.detail: The reviewer has only Read/Glob/Grep/Write and no Bash; it cannot rename a file, and under dontAsk a temp-file write would be denied even with a single-path allow rule. PR 11's prompt explicitly says the file cannot be written under a temporary name and renamed. Another symptom of never exercising the prompt live.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:168: 'On completion write the following JSON shape atomically (temporary file then rename) to …'. Contrast /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-ultra/workflow/automatic.py:175-176: 'It cannot be written under a temporary name and renamed, so write it once, complete, as your last action'.

findings.title: Deadline does not stop the reviewer, departing from 'same lifecycle as workers'; recorded
findings.detail: PRD §1/§2 ask for the same lifecycle as workers, and workers are stopped when their deadline expires. PR 9 raises at the deadline but leaves the reviewer running for the operator to stop. Justified in the handoff (an idle reviewer consumes no usage) and stated in the RUNBOOK recovery entry, so class (a). PR 10 and PR 11 stop it.
findings.evidence: PR 9 RUNBOOK diff: 'A reviewer left idle after a deadline is not stopped for you; stop it with its recorded native ID'. Handoff 'Decisions and deviations': 'A deadline does not stop the reviewer.' automatic.py:202-203 raises without stop; the BaseException handler (288-292) only updates the receipt. Contrast PR 10 automatic.py:305-313 and PR 11 automatic.py:349-356.

findings.title: Exact scope discipline, repo-convention contract, and candid status reporting
findings.detail: PR 9 touches only the slice-A file set the PRD names, defines reviewCompletion in v1.ts with examples and negative contract tests and generates the JSON via the repo's export script, ticks the three-pane open question in both PRDs, adds an explicit PRD §7 note for the Write-tool deviation, and states in the PRD status line, handoff and PR body that the smoke gate was not run. Its handoff also documents three mutation checks. That transparency is exactly what the dimension asks for, even though the delivered behaviour falls short.
findings.evidence: `git diff --stat 61e4752 feature-opus`: 21 files, no server/ or src/. contracts/workflow/v1.ts:94-106, contract.test.ts:56-78, contracts/workflow/README.md row for reviewCompletion. docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md (PR 9) §7 'Implementation note'; umbrella decisions log '[x] Three-pane layout: same tab, created when the review node starts (slice A, implemented)'. HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md 'Mutation checks' table.

findings.title: B and C pre-run work bundled into slice A's PR against the umbrella's 'each slice ships on its own'
findings.detail: The umbrella says slice A ships alone as an ordinary commit and that C 'Depends on: B merged'. PR 10 ships A plus both slices' pre-run tables (contracts/projects reviewResult 1.1.0 and runInputs 1.2.0, export 1.2.0, `workflow export`, two feature directories) in one squashed commit, doing C's pre-run work before B has even been launched. The content matches what PRD_REVIEW_RESULT §2 and PRD_RUN_INPUTS §3 ask for, and the handoff proposes a three-commit split, but the PR is one commit so a reviewer of slice A must read +3329 lines.
findings.evidence: docs/PRD_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:17-21 (main): 'A … ordinary commit', 'C … Depends on: B merged', 'Order: A, then B's run, then C's run'. `git diff --numstat 61e4752 feature-high`: contracts +1393/-7, features +607/-4. /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md 'Suggested commits' 1-3 and 'Committed as one change on 2026-09-22'.

findings.title: Export bumped to 1.2.0 with main's adapter pinned to 1.0.0; new runs (including B's own run) become unviewable until B's adapter lands
findings.detail: PR 10 changes EXPORT_VERSION to 1.2.0 without touching server/, while main's adapter validates `version: z.literal('1.0.0')`. After merge every newly prepared run, including the review-result feature run the PRD wants next, is rejected by the viewer until that run's adapter task merges. The PRD's own pre-run design has this gap for 1.1.0, but PR 10 widened it to 1.2.0 and moved it from 'right before B's run' to 'at A's merge'. Disclosed in the PR body and handoff; the existing live run is safe because it is not re-exported (its run-state.json is still the 1.0.0 shape).
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/export_state.py:16 `EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0"`; `git diff --stat 61e4752 feature-high -- server/ src/` is empty. /home/agentops/dev/md-manager/server/projects.ts:37 `const EXPORT_VERSION = '1.0.0'`, :52 `version: z.literal(EXPORT_VERSION)`. PR body 'Not done here': 'New runs export at 1.2.0 until B's adapter lands.' Live run: `python3 -c` on ~/.local/state/…/project-workflows-001/run-state.json shows keys version/run_id/…/verification_packets with no review/inputs section. Contrast PR 11 server/projects.ts:44 `EXPORT_VERSIONS = ['1.0.0', '1.1.0', '1.2.0']`.

findings.title: Completion accepted in native state `blocked`, while PRD row and PR 10's own RUNBOOK say idle or done
findings.detail: wait_review accepts the file when the session is idle, done or blocked; the PRD's 'Accepted when' row and PR 10's RUNBOOK sentence both say idle or done. The rationale (an answer typed in the pane can still lead to the file) is only in a test comment. Minor, but it is the one PR 10 deviation not written into the PRDs.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:211: `if row["state"] in {"idle", "done", "blocked"} and path.exists():`. RUNBOOK (PR 10 diff): 'The file is accepted only once the session is `idle` or `done`'. test_automatic.py:567-570: '# An answer in the pane can still lead to the file; it is accepted in the blocked state too.' PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:28 row unchanged.

findings.title: Plans without reviewer_transport default to print, versus PRD 'Default is the native session'; justified and recorded
findings.detail: reviewer_transport(plan) returns 'print' when the key is absent because such plans were prepared before the native reviewer existed and were in fact reviewed in print mode; prepare pins 'native' for every new run so the user-facing default is native. Recorded in the RUNBOOK and handoff. PR 9 and PR 11 default missing keys to native (PR 11 then records null/actual transport in the export).
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:43-45 with comment 'Runs prepared before the native reviewer existed carry no transport key; they were reviewed in print mode.' DEFAULTS line 26 `"reviewer_transport": "native"`. RUNBOOK: 'Runs prepared before this transport existed are treated as print-mode runs.' PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md:17 'Default is the native session.'

findings.title: Spec-literal UUID binding relies on the reviewer knowing its own session id; a mis-copy ends the run
findings.detail: To bind the reviewer session UUID as the PRD table demands, the prompt asks the reviewer to write 'your own session UUID as shown by `claude agents`', but the reviewer has no Bash. The live transcript shows it wrote the correct UUID without running `claude agents` or reading review.interactive.json (39 Read calls, none of the receipt), so the model's self-knowledge carried it. If a reviewer ever writes a wrong UUID, read_review_completion raises, the run is blocked and no second reviewer is launched. Faithful to the spec; fragile in practice. PR 9 and PR 11 sidestep this with a controller-issued launch token.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:159: `"reviewer_session": "<your own session UUID as shown by `claude agents`; the controller verifies it>"`; 184-185 rejects a mismatch.
